title: WPMS/324/2013 of MOHAN SINGH RANA Vs KRISHI UTPADAN MANDI SAMITY and OTHERS

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition No.324 of 2013 (M/S)
Mohan Singh Rana. ÖÖPetitioner
Versus
The Krishi Utpadan Mandi Samity
Naveen Mandi Sthal and others ...ÖRespondents
Mr. Harendra Belwal, Advocates for the petitioner.
Mr. J.C. Belwal, Advocate for the respondent nos.1 to 3.
Mr. Vipul Sharma, Advocate for the respondent no.5.
Dated: July 18, 2013
Honíble V.K. Bist, J.
 Present petition has been filed by the petitioner
for the following reliefs:
ìa. Issue a writ, order or direction in the
nature of mandamus commanding the
respondents make allotment of canteen no.5 in
favour of the petitioner being second highest
bidder.
 b. Issue a writ, order or direction in the
nature of certiorari quashing the impugned
condition of six months character certificate
given in the tender form.
 c. Any other order or direction, which this
Honíble Court may deem fit and proper in the
circumstances of the case.
 d. Award the cost of writ petition.î
2. In the month of December, 2012, tender was
invited for allotment of canteen no.5 situated in the
premises of Mandi Samity Parisar Haldwani, district
Nainital. The application of the person, who was the
highest bidder, was rejected on the ground that he did
not fulfill the terms and condition of tender. The
petitioner submitted his tender in time and his offer
was found second highest, but his offer was not
accepted, as along with his offer, the petitioner did not

2
annex his character certificate. In the tender notice, it
was mentioned that a person willing for allotment of
canteen, is required to annex certain documents with
his offer. One of the conditions for the aforesaid
allotment was that the character certificate for the
allotment issued not earlier than six months had to be
submitted along with the tender.
3. The contention of the learned counsel for the
petitioner is that due to strike of ministerial staff in the
Collectorate, the character certificate was not issued to
the petitioner and therefore, the petitioner could not
submit his latest character certificate.
4. The respondents have filed counter affidavit. In
the counter affidavit, it is stated that other persons,
namely, Santosh Kabadwal, Deepak Gautam and
Ashok Kapoor were issued character certificates on
15.01.2013, and the petitioner could have also
obtained the same.
5. Mr. J.C. Belwal, Advocate for the respondent
nos.1 to 3 submitted that since the petitioner did not
comply the condition of the tender and did not submit
the character certificate in accordance with the term
and condition of tender, the respondent nos.1 to 3 have
rightly rejected the offer of the petitioner and have
rightly given contract to the next highest bidder i.e.
respondent no.5.

3
6. Mr. Vipul Sharma, Advocate for the respondent
no.5 relied upon the judgment passed by the Honíble
Supreme Court in the case of ìRam Gajadhar Nishad
Vs. State of U.P. and othersî reported in (1990) 2
Supreme Court Cases 486. He submitted that though
the petitioner offer was higher but it could not have
been considered, inasmuch as, he did not fulfill the
basic mandatory condition of filing the character
certificate along with the tender form.
7. I have perused the judgment relied by the learned
counsel for the respondent no.5. The judgment cited by
the learned counsel for the respondent no.5 squarely
covers the controversy involved in the present writ
petition. In the case of the petitioner, the petitioner did
not fulfill the mandatory condition of tender notice, viz.
filing of latest character certificate before the last date
of submission of tender. Therefore, his tender was
rightly rejected.
8. In view of above discussion, the writ petition is
dismissed. However, the amount deposited by the
petitioner shall be refunded to him within a period of
one month from today, if rules provides for the same.
9. No order as to costs.
 (V.K. Bist, J.)
Arpan 18.07.2013
